newsitem.title: SPAIN: POLL-Bank of Spain seen holding rate to mid-June.
newsitem.headline: POLL-Bank of Spain seen holding rate to mid-June.

text.p: The Bank of Spain probably will not reduce its key 5.25 percent money market rate on Friday but is likely to lower it as soon as the second half of June, analysts said on Thursday.
Of 11 experts and market dealers polled by Reuters on Thursday, none expected expected a cut tomorrow.
But 10 forecast that the fifth 25-basis-point reduction in the Spanish official rate this year would take place in the second part of the next month.
Some added that the most likely date was at the Bank of Spain's repo on June 16, the first one after the announcement of May CPI figures set for release on June 13.
"At present there is not any reason why they should not reduce their official rate after CPI," said Jose Ramon Arechederra, dealer at ABN-AMRO in Madrid.
After a sharp fall in the Spanish inflation rate at the beginning of the year, dealers expect that Spanish CPI could fall more in May.
"We expect the May CPI to fall to around 1.5 percent year-on-year versus 1.7 percent in April," said Maria Victoria Nunez at Societe Generale in Madrid.

The Bank of Spain last cut its official rate by 25 basis points to 5.25 percent on May 16. It started the current easing cycle on December 1995 when it cut the rate by 25 basis points from 9.25 percent.
"We expect them to cut once more by 25 basis points, than hold the repo rate at 5.0 percent trough the second part of the year," said Francesco Giordano analyst at CSFB in London.
